risks.risk_description: Cybersecurity is a ubiquitous concern with organizations facing high or very high risk due to increasing threats and vulnerabilities in their IT environments.

risk_driver.driver_description: The reliance on complex IT systems and third-party IT services increases exposure to cyber threats.
Cyber threats are continuously evolving, making it challenging to maintain effective defenses.

risk_recommendations: Increase audit frequency to at least annually or continuously to monitor cybersecurity risks effectively.
Integrate cybersecurity considerations into broader audit engagements.
Invest in technology and staff training to enhance cybersecurity posture.
risks.trend: Cybersecurity remains the number one risk area with 78% of respondents rating it as high or very high risk. Audit allocation for cybersecurity has increased since 2019 and remains elevated.
risks.likelihood: High, with 78% of organizations rating it as high or very high risk.
risks.impact: Potential for severe operational disruption, data breaches, financial loss, and reputational damage.
risks.risk_indicator: Frequency of cybersecurity incidents and audit coverage frequency.
contextual_variations: Cybersecurity risk levels are slightly lower in publicly traded organizations compared to financial services.
Smaller internal audit functions have reduced audit frequency for cybersecurity.

risks.risk_description: Risks related to IT systems other than cybersecurity, including system failures, data integrity issues, and technology obsolescence.

risk_driver.driver_description: Diverse and piecemeal IT systems increase complexity and risk.
Technical and cost challenges associated with migrating to cloud platforms.

risk_recommendations: Increase audit focus on IT systems and infrastructure.
Invest in upgrading and integrating IT systems to support operational efficiency.
Address supply chain challenges impacting IT investments.
risks.trend: IT risk is the second highest risk area with 46% rating it as high or very high risk. Audit allocation for IT has increased slightly since 2019.
risks.likelihood: Moderate to high, with 46% rating it as high or very high risk.
risks.impact: Operational disruptions, inefficiencies, and potential financial losses.
risks.risk_indicator: Audit frequency and IT incident reports.
contextual_variations: Publicly traded organizations rate IT risk slightly lower than financial services.
Smaller audit functions have less frequent IT audits.

risks.risk_description: Risks arising from reliance on third-party vendors and service providers, especially in IT services.

risk_driver.driver_description: Dependence on third parties for critical IT functions increases exposure to external risks.
Audit frequency for third-party relationships is lower than the perceived risk level.

risk_recommendations: Increase audit frequency to align with risk levels, ideally at least every 5 years or more frequently.
Implement robust third-party risk management frameworks.
Monitor and assess third-party controls regularly.
risks.trend: Third-party relationships rank as the third highest risk area with 44% rating it as high or very high risk, but only 58% audit it at least every 5 years, indicating a gap.
risks.impact: Potential operational disruptions, compliance failures, and reputational damage due to third-party failures.
risks.risk_indicator: Audit frequency and third-party incident reports.
contextual_variations: Privately held organizations rate third-party relationships as the second highest risk area.

risks.risk_description: Risks related to the accuracy and reliability of financial reporting and internal controls over financial reporting.

risk_driver.driver_description: Compliance with Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) and other financial reporting regulations.
Complexity in financial reporting processes increases risk of errors.

risk_recommendations: Maintain strong internal controls and regular SOX compliance audits.
Allocate sufficient audit resources to financial reporting areas.
Continuously monitor changes in financial reporting standards.
risks.trend: Financial reporting remains a significant risk, especially for publicly traded organizations, with audit allocation averaging 31%. However, allocation has decreased slightly since last year.
risks.likelihood: High in publicly traded organizations due to regulatory requirements.
risks.impact: Financial misstatements, regulatory penalties, and reputational damage.
risks.risk_indicator: SOX compliance status and audit coverage.
contextual_variations: Publicly traded organizations have higher audit allocation for financial reporting compared to other sectors.
Privately held organizations implementing SOX allocate more audit resources to financial reporting.

risks.risk_description: Risks related to non-compliance with laws, regulations, and policies outside of financial reporting controls.

risk_driver.driver_description: Growing complexity and volume of regulatory requirements.

risk_recommendations: Conduct regular compliance audits and assessments.
Implement robust compliance management systems.
Stay updated on regulatory changes and adapt policies accordingly.
risks.trend: Compliance risk is rated high or very high by 37% of respondents, with audit frequency generally aligned but with some gaps.
risks.impact: Legal penalties, operational disruptions, and reputational harm.
risks.risk_indicator: Compliance audit results and regulatory incident reports.
contextual_variations: Publicly traded organizations rate compliance risk slightly lower than financial services.

risks.risk_description: Risks arising from failures in internal processes, people, and systems affecting day-to-day operations.

risk_driver.driver_description: Inefficient or outdated processes increase operational risk.
Errors, fraud, or lack of training among staff.

risk_recommendations: Enhance process controls and automation.
Provide staff training and awareness programs.
Regularly review and update operational procedures.
risks.trend: Operational risk is rated high or very high by 30% of respondents, with audit allocation varying by sector.
risks.impact: Operational disruptions, financial losses, and reputational damage.
risks.risk_indicator: Operational incident frequency and audit findings.
contextual_variations: Public sector and nonprofit organizations allocate more audit effort to operational risks.

risks.risk_description: Risks related to intentional acts of deception for personal or organizational gain.

risk_driver.driver_description: Inadequate internal controls increase fraud risk.
Financial pressures may motivate fraudulent behavior.

risk_recommendations: Implement strong anti-fraud controls and monitoring.
Conduct regular fraud risk assessments and investigations.
Promote ethical culture and whistleblower programs.
risks.trend: Fraud risk is rated high or very high by 24% of respondents, with audit frequency generally aligned.
risks.impact: Financial losses, legal consequences, and reputational damage.
risks.risk_indicator: Number of fraud incidents and investigation outcomes.

risks.risk_description: Risks related to ineffective governance structures and poor organizational culture impacting decision-making and compliance.

risk_driver.driver_description: Lack of strong leadership and oversight.
Unethical behavior or lack of accountability.

risk_recommendations: Strengthen governance frameworks and oversight mechanisms.
Promote ethical culture and accountability.
Integrate governance considerations into audits.
risks.trend: Governance and culture risk is rated high or very high by 21% of respondents, with audit frequency lower than risk level indicating a gap.
risks.impact: Poor decision-making, compliance failures, and reputational harm.
risks.risk_indicator: Governance audit findings and culture assessments.

risks.risk_description: Risks associated with the need to reduce costs and expenses, potentially impacting operations and strategic initiatives.
risk_recommendations: Conduct audits focused on cost management and efficiency.
Implement strategic cost reduction plans without compromising quality.
Monitor impact of cost reductions on operations.
risks.trend: Cost/expense reduction risk is trending up since 2020 and is rated high or very high by 20% of respondents.
risks.impact: Potential operational disruptions and reduced service quality.
risks.risk_indicator: Cost reduction audit results and financial performance metrics.
contextual_variations: Cost/expense reduction risk is higher in nonprofit and privately held organizations.

risks.risk_description: Risks related to sustainability initiatives and non-financial reporting, including environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors.

risk_driver.driver_description: Increasing demands for transparency and sustainability performance.

risk_recommendations: Increase audit focus on sustainability and non-financial reporting.
Develop robust ESG reporting frameworks.
Engage stakeholders on sustainability goals.
risks.trend: Sustainability risk is increasing, with notable audit allocation increases since 2019 and moderate to high risk ratings in public sector and nonprofit organizations.
risks.impact: Reputational damage and regulatory penalties if sustainability goals are not met.
risks.risk_indicator: Sustainability audit coverage and ESG performance metrics.
contextual_variations: Higher risk perception in public sector and nonprofit organizations.

risks.risk_description: Risks related to the adequacy of support provided to external auditors, impacting audit quality and compliance.

risk_driver.driver_description: Limited internal resources to support external audit processes.

risk_recommendations: Ensure adequate resources and coordination for external audits.
Integrate support activities into internal audit plans.
risks.trend: Support for external audit is audited more frequently than the perceived risk level, indicating proactive management.
risks.impact: Potential delays or issues in external audit processes.

risks.risk_name: Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) and Related Processes
risks.risk_description: Risks associated with the effectiveness of ERM frameworks and related risk management processes.

risk_driver.driver_description: Variability in the maturity and integration of ERM processes.

risk_recommendations: Regularly assess and improve ERM frameworks.
Integrate ERM considerations into audit plans.
Enhance risk identification and mitigation processes.
risks.trend: ERM risk is rated moderate to high by a significant portion of respondents, with audit frequency somewhat aligned.
risks.impact: Inadequate risk management leading to unmitigated exposures.
risks.risk_indicator: ERM audit findings and risk assessment results.
